question:
Evaluate the following.

sin 25° sin 65° – cos 25° cos 65°.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert 65° to its complementary angle.

⇒ sin 65° = cos(90° − 65°) = cos 25°

⇒ cos 65° = sin(90° − 65°) = sin 25°

Substitute these into the given expression:

⇒ sin 25° cos 25° − cos 25° sin 25° = 0

**∴ The correct answer is 0.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

sin 25° sin 65° − cos 25° cos 65°

**Formula Used:**

cos(A + B) = cos A cos B − sin A sin B

**Calculation:**

⇒ Re-write the given expression by taking the negative sign common:

⇒ − (cos 25° cos 65° − sin 25° sin 65°)

⇒ Apply the formula taking A = 25° and B = 65°

⇒ − cos(25° + 65°)

⇒ − cos(90°)

⇒ Since cos(90°) = 0

⇒ 0

**∴ The correct answer is 0.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Complementary Angles

sin(90° − θ) = cos θ | cos(90° − θ) = sin θ | tan(90° − θ) = cot θ

Trigonometric Sum & Difference Formulas

sin(A + B) = sin A cos B + cos A sin B | cos(A − B) = cos A cos B + sin A sin B

Double Angle Formulas

sin 2A = 2 sin A cos A | cos 2A = cos² A − sin² A
